claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or its high-entropy derivatives have coercivity no greater than 100 Oe.
Controlled plastic deformation or thermomechanical processing can trigger a partial fcc-to-hcp transformation in FeCoNi.
Processing below the full-recrystallization regime can nucleate a minor, dispersed hcp phase in FeCoNi.
The intervention will form nanoscale hcp precipitates within the fcc FeCoNi matrix.
The hcp precipitates will have semi-coherent boundaries with the fcc matrix.
The emergent hcp phase will have higher magnetocrystalline anisotropy than the fcc phase.
Interfaces between the hcp regions and fcc matrix will impede magnetic domain-wall motion.
Domain-wall pinning by the hcp regions will increase coercivity relative to the starting single-phase fcc state.
The processed material may attain coercivity well above approximately 100 Oe.
A sufficient and uniform distribution of hcp precipitates is required for the predicted coercivity increase.
Equiatomic CrCoNi can undergo an fcc-to-hcp phase transformation.
The fcc-to-hcp transformation in CrCoNi is triggered by dislocation slip and interaction with internal boundaries.
In CrCoNi, the fcc-to-hcp transformation increases strength without compromising plastic deformation.
The CrCoNi study supports transformation-induced magnetic domain-wall pinning.
Avoiding complete hcp transformation is necessary to prevent mechanical embrittlement in the proposed FeCoNi treatment.

contradictions.description: The initial state and baseline permit either FeCoNi or a high-entropy derivative, whereas the boundary says the intervention should be applied only within the FeCoNi compositional window.
